settings.unknownAddressText: You knock, you ask, you look about — but nobody here knows anything of clocks, ledgers or missing apprentices.

watch.name: Engraved pocket watch
watch.description: A silver hunter-case watch, stopped at twenty past nine. The case is engraved **M.R.** — it is not Elias Thorne's.

cipher.name: Scrap of paper
cipher.description: Found under the workbench at Thorne's shop. Written in Tom Hale's hand:

ledger.name: Thorne's service ledger
ledger.description: Every clock Elias Thorne has regulated this year — including the vault time-lock at the London & County Bank.

content.title: March
content.text:
4th — St. Bride's turret clock. Cleaned & oiled.
9th — Mrs Abernathy, carriage clock, new mainspring.
12th — **London & County Bank, 3 EC.** Vault time-lock regulated. Next release: **Saturday 16th, nine o'clock in the evening**, for the bullion transfer.

content.title: Bullion On The Move
content.text:
The London & County Bank of Lombard Street is understood to be preparing a considerable transfer of gold bullion to its Paris correspondents this weekend. The bank declined to name the hour.

SHOPKEEPERS of the City are warned of a gang of housebreakers active in the district these past weeks. Inspector Lestrade of Scotland Yard declares the matter well in hand.

TO LET — Warehouse space at Cooper's Wharf, Southwark. Apply within.
Not every place in London is in the directory.
I saw two men take the ledger from Mr Thorne's bench on Tuesday night. One had a scar from his eye to his chin. The other was Mr Reed the pawnbroker. They saw me. I ran.

intro: The fog has not lifted from Baker Street all morning when a telegram arrives.

intro.to: To: Mr Sherlock Holmes, 221B Baker Street
intro.text: SHOP BROKEN INTO TUESDAY NIGHT STOP NOTHING OF VALUE TAKEN STOP MY APPRENTICE TOM HALE MISSING SINCE STOP POLICE UNINTERESTED STOP PLEASE COME

intro: Holmes reads it twice and tosses it to you across the breakfast things.

intro.text: A burglar who breaks into a clockmaker's and takes no clocks. An apprentice who vanishes the same night. I am occupied with the Abernathy affair — you will go in my place. Find out **what was taken**, **why**, and **when the thieves mean to use it**.
intro.speaker: Sherlock Holmes

reed-bluff: You lean across the counter and mention, quite casually, that Inspector Lestrade is a personal friend.

reed-bluff.text: All right, all right! I only bought what they brought me. The boy — Hale — he's hiding at the old Cooper's warehouse, down at **21 SE**. Scarface wants him found before Saturday. That's all I know!
reed-bluff.speaker: Marcus Reed

1 WC.name: Scotland Yard
content: Inspector Lestrade receives you with the air of a man interrupted at lunch.

content.text: Thorne? Nothing stolen, no crime. As for his apprentice — boys run off every day of the week. Here, if it'll make you go away:
content.speaker: Inspector Lestrade

content.caption: Reported break-ins, City of London, March

content.text: You show him the watch engraved *M.R.* He shrugs. “Could be anyone's. Ask the Clockmakers' Company — they keep a register of engravers' marks.”

3 EC.name: London & County Bank
content: The manager, a narrow man in a narrow coat, will discuss nothing with strangers — until you mention Elias Thorne.

content.text: Thorne regulates the time-lock on our vault. Once it is set, not even I can open the door until the hour arrives. A marvellous mechanism. As to *when* it next opens — that, sir, is precisely the sort of thing we do not tell people.
content.speaker: The bank manager

content.text: When you show him the ledger, he goes very pale indeed, and sends a clerk running for the police.

12 EC.name: Thorne's Clock Shop
content: Ten thousand ticks greet you as you step inside. Elias Thorne is a stooped man with magnifying spectacles pushed up onto his forehead.

content.text: They turned the place over, but not one clock is missing. Only my service ledger — and who would want that? And Tom… Tom has never missed a day.
content.speaker: Elias Thorne

content: On the workbench lies a silver pocket watch. Thorne swears it isn't his.
Wedged between the floorboards is a scrap of paper in Tom's handwriting. Thorne says the boy was forever reading about Julius Caesar.

content.hint: Caesar is said to have shifted every letter of his messages **three places** along the alphabet. Shift each letter three places *back*: P→M, H→E…
content.wrongText: That doesn't read as English yet.

content: **MEET ME AT THE RAVEN.** Thorne knows it — a public house round the corner, at **33 EC**. It isn't in the directory.

26 EC.name: The Times
content: A harassed sub-editor confirms the bullion story came from a clerk at the bank. “They'd never print the hour, of course. Half of London would turn up.”

33 EC.name: The Raven
content: A low, smoky public house. The regulars fall silent as you enter.

blocks: You mention Tom Hale's name to the barmaid, and the note he left. Her face softens.

blocks.text: Tom? He was in Tuesday, white as a sheet, waiting on someone who never came. A man with a scar from his eye to his chin was asking after him later — him and **Reed the pawnbroker**. Thick as thieves, those two.
blocks.speaker: The barmaid

else.text: Nobody here will talk to a stranger who doesn't know why they've come. Perhaps there's something you've missed.

47 EC.name: Worshipful Company of Clockmakers
content: A dusty register of engravers' marks fills an entire wall.

content.text: The clerk turns the pages for you. The mark on your watch belongs to a watch once pawned and never redeemed at the shop of **Marcus Reed, pawnbroker, 58 E** — Reed has been using it himself.

else.text: Without something to look up, the register is just a wall of names.

58 E.name: Reed's Pawnshop
content: Behind a counter of tarnished candlesticks and stopped clocks stands a man with very quick eyes.

blocks: At the mention of Tom Hale, his quick eyes stop moving.

blocks.prompt: How will you make him talk? (You only get one chance.)

actions.label: Hint that Lestrade is a close friend
Slide a half-crown across the counter
then: Reed pockets the coin without looking at it. “Hale? Try Cooper's Wharf. **21 SE**.” He doesn't meet your eye — and you suspect he'll tell Scarface you've been asking.

actions.label: Grab his collar and demand answers
then: Reed shouts for help. A very large man appears from the back room and you find yourself in the gutter outside. That was a mistake.

else.text: Reed sells you nothing and tells you less. You have no reason to press him — yet.

21 SE.name: Cooper's Wharf
content: Rows of empty warehouses lean over the black water of the Thames.

blocks: In the third warehouse, behind a stack of rotting barrels, you find a frightened boy of fifteen. It's Tom Hale.

blocks.text: They took the ledger — the scarred man and Mr Reed. I saw them. I've been too scared to go home.
blocks.speaker: Tom Hale

effects.notify: Tom's statement added to your tools.

blocks: Tom says the gang uses the last warehouse on the wharf. There may still be time to search it — but if their lookout sees you, you won't get a second chance.

actions.label: Search the gang's warehouse
actions.confirm: Once you search, the gang's lookout will spot you and you can't come back here. Go ahead?
then: You slip through a broken shutter. On a crate, beside a half-eaten pie, lies Thorne's ledger — open at a page that has been circled in pencil.

content.text: 12th — **London & County Bank, 3 EC.** Vault time-lock regulated. Next release: **Saturday 16th, nine o'clock in the evening**, for the bullion transfer.

then: A whistle shrieks outside. You run.

actions.label: Leave for now
then: You decide to come back later.

else.text: There are dozens of warehouses. Without knowing which one, you could search for a week.

9 NW.name: Mrs Thorne's house
content: Ada Thorne hands you a letter delivered by a street boy on Wednesday morning.

content.text: Please tell Mr Thorne I am safe and I am sorry. I saw what they took and I know what it is for. I will come back when it is safe.
The letter has no address. Whatever Tom saw, he thought it was worth hiding over.

questions.text: What was taken from Thorne's shop, and why did the thieves want it?
questions.answerText: Thorne's service ledger — it recorded when the London & County Bank's vault time-lock would next open.

options.text: Saturday at nine in the evening

questions.explanation: The circled ledger entry gives the next release of the vault's time-lock.

questions.text: What is Marcus Reed's part in the plot?

options.text: None — he simply bought a stolen watch
He took the ledger with the scarred man, and fences for the gang
He is Tom Hale's uncle, sheltering him

rules.label: Got Reed talking without paying him
Roughed up Reed (and got thrown out)

ratings.label: Back to Baker Street with you.

content: Holmes listens to your report with his fingertips pressed together.

content.text: A clockmaker's ledger is a timetable of other people's secrets. The gang never wanted Thorne's clocks — they wanted to know the one hour when the London & County's vault would open itself: **nine o'clock on Saturday evening**, during the bullion transfer. Reed fenced for them and lent his watch to the job; it fell from his pocket in the dark. Young Hale saw everything, left a note for Thorne in the only cipher he knew, and ran. Lestrade will be waiting at the bank on Saturday. Well done.
content.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
